title: 〜合う "do to each other / together"
meaning: Reciprocal action between two or more people.
simpleExplanation: V-ます stem + 合う means "do to each other / do together": 話し合う (talk with each other, discuss), 助け合う (help each other), 知り合う (get to know each other). 合う on its own means "to fit / to match", so the compound shows that two or more people's actions fit together. The partner is marked with と, or the subject is plural (二人は, みんなで).
whenUsed: Talking about relationships and cooperation: discussions (話し合う), mutual support (助け合う), meeting people (知り合う, 付き合う = go out with / keep company with), and arranging to meet (待ち合わせる). Common in speeches about teamwork and in everyday stories about friends.
formation: V-ます stem + 合う: 話す → 話し合う, 助ける → 助け合う, 知る → 知り合う, 愛する → 愛し合う
Partner with と: 友達と話し合う; or plural subject: 二人は助け合った
Conjugates as Group 1: 合います / 合った / 合って
Note: 間に合う (be in time) and 似合う (suit) are not reciprocal

parts.role: V-stem + 合う: did it to each other

diagram.translation: I discussed opinions with my friend (we talked with each other).

examples.ja: 友達と意見を話し合いました。
examples.reading: ともだちと いけんを はなしあいました。
examples.en: I discussed opinions with my friend.
examples.note: 話す → 話し合う: both sides talk; 友達と marks the partner.

examples.ja: 困ったときは助け合いましょう。
examples.reading: こまった ときは たすけあいましょう。
examples.en: Let's help each other when in trouble.
examples.note: 助ける → 助け合う: mutual help, with ましょう as a call to cooperate.

examples.ja: 二人は駅で待ち合わせた。
examples.reading: ふたりは えきで まちあわせた。
examples.en: The two arranged to meet at the station.
examples.note: 待ち合わせる (transitive 合わせる): arrange to meet; the two are the plural subject.

examples.ja: 二人は大学で知り合って、三年後に結婚した。
examples.reading: ふたりは だいがくで しりあって、さんねんごに けっこんした。
examples.en: The two met at university and married three years later.
examples.note: 知り合う = get to know each other; plural subject 二人は.

examples.ja: 問題があるときは、家族でよく話し合ったほうがいい。
examples.reading: もんだいが あるときは、かぞくで よく はなしあったほうが いい。
examples.en: When there is a problem, it's better for the family to talk it over together.
examples.note: 家族で (as a family) makes the group the joint subject.

similarGrammar.difference: The adverb "each other" can add the same meaning to any verb (お互いに助ける). 〜合う builds the meaning into the verb itself.
一緒に食べる = eat together (side by side). 〜合う means the action is directed at each other.
合う (intransitive: match) / 合わせる (transitive: put together) is one such pair; 待ち合わせる uses the transitive side.

commonMistakes.why: The partner of a reciprocal action takes と (with), not に.

commonMistakes.wrong: 私は電車に間に合い合った。
commonMistakes.right: 私は電車に間に合った。
commonMistakes.why: 間に合う (be in time) already contains 合う and is not reciprocal; do not add another 合う.
合う attaches to the ます-stem.

usageNotes: Common compounds: 話し合う, 助け合う, 知り合う, 付き合う, 言い合う (argue), 笑い合う, 分かり合う (understand each other), 支え合う (support each other).
The noun forms are common too: 話し合い (a discussion), 知り合い (an acquaintance), 付き合い (relationship / socialising).
待ち合わせ (meeting arrangement) is a noun made from the transitive 合わせる: 駅で待ち合わせをする.
jlptTips: A partner marked with と or a plural subject (二人は, みんなで, お互いに) plus a verb blank suggests 〜合う.
Watch for non-reciprocal 合う words in the options: 間に合う (be in time), 似合う (suit), 気が合う (get along). Meaning, not form, decides.
